name: @cloudgrid-io/mcp

tools.name: grid_pickup
tools.description: Pick up an app: make your OWN COPY of any app you can see (like a git fork) into a grid you can build in. It mints a NEW entity with lineage back to the source and WITHOUT the source's secrets (set your own before you plug). Plugging your copy creates/updates YOUR entity — the original is never touched. Requires sign-in. This is a FORK, not a "collab": it never grants you access to anyone else's live entity. Getting PUSH ACCESS to the SAME entity is a different operation — the grid_collab tool (or the CLI `grid collab <entity>`) — so do NOT reach for grid_pickup when the user asks to collab; reach for grid_collab. To edit the ORIGINAL entity in place (as its owner or a collaborator), use grid_pull instead.

entity_id.description: The source app to copy: a canonical UUID or <grid-slug>/<entity-slug>.

grid.description: Grid to create your copy in. Required only when you belong to more than one grid.

name.description: Slug for your copy. Omit to derive one from the source.

source_version_id.description: Copy an older version instead of HEAD, e.g. v_a1b2c3d.

tools.name: grid_pull
tools.description: Pull an app to continue/edit it IN PLACE — like `git clone` of the SAME entity: your next grid_plug (with its target_entity_id) updates that entity, and the team sees the new version. Requires PUSH ACCESS: you must own it or be a collaborator. If you can only view it, you CANNOT edit or plug it — say so, and offer the two real options: (1) make your own separate copy (a fork) with grid_pickup, or (2) GET push access to the SAME entity with grid_collab (or the CLI `grid collab <entity>`) — "collab" is a distinct access-control operation that grants permission only and fetches nothing, so once it is granted you run grid_pull again to get the code (and if the owner gates access, grid_collab becomes a request they approve). A drop plugged outside any grid is claimed into the grid you choose by passing its `claim_token`; only the drop's owner can claim it. Requires sign-in. Calls the API directly (both editions).

entity_id.description: The entity id to pull. Defaults to the drop made outside a grid in this session, if any.

grid.description: Grid to resolve a bare slug in. Required only when you belong to more than one grid.

claim_token.description: Claiming a drop plugged outside a grid: its owner token — claims that drop into your grid. Only the drop's owner can claim it.

claim_url.description: Alternative to claim_token — the claim_url from the plug result; the token is read from it.

tools.name: grid_collab
tools.description: Collab: GET PUSH ACCESS to the SAME live entity that someone else owns — you become a collaborator on THAT entity, not a copy. This grants PERMISSION ONLY and fetches nothing: after it succeeds, run grid_pull to get the code, then grid_plug (with its target_entity_id) updates the SHARED entity in place (the team sees the new version and can roll it back). This is NOT a fork — it never mints a new entity and never carries forked_from lineage; if you want your OWN separate copy instead, that is grid_pickup. If the owner GATES who may join, this does NOT dead-end: it sends the owner a request for access on your behalf, and once they approve, access is live immediately — no need to re-run grid_collab. Use this — not grid_pickup — whenever the user asks to "collab" on, "join", or "get push/write access to" an app they don't own. Requires sign-in. Calls the API directly (both editions).

entity_id.description: The app to get push access to: a canonical UUID or <grid-slug>/<entity-slug>.

grid.description: Grid to resolve a bare slug in. Required only when a bare slug is ambiguous across grids you belong to.

tools.name: grid_create_grid
tools.description: Create a new grid (workspace) for the signed-in user — they become its admin. Use when the account has no grid yet (grid_plug returns needs_grid_create, or a plug fails with NO_ACTIVE_ORG): suggest a short slug from the user's name or app, CONFIRM it with the user (the slug is permanent and appears in URLs), create, then call grid_plug with grid: <slug>. A brand-new grid provisions in the background (~30s); grid_plug waits for readiness before deploying, so call it right away — no manual delay or polling needed. Never send the user to the console to create a grid by hand. Requires sign-in. Calls the API directly (both editions).

slug.description: The grid slug: 3-40 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens, starting with a letter. Permanent — confirm with the user before creating.

tools.name: grid_note
tools.description: Leave a one-paragraph summary of what you built this session and why, for the local edition's optional QA session log, which the CloudGrid team reads. Call it BEFORE a plug, or in a session that ends without one — a successful plug posts the log on that same call, so pass grid_plug's session_note instead. The log is dark unless the operator of this machine has set CLOUDGRID_QA_SLACK_WEBHOOK.

summary.description: A short plain-language summary of what was built and why.

tools.name: grid_plug
tools.description: Plug an app, website, game, or single HTML page into CloudGrid and get a live public URL in seconds. Serves requests to deploy, publish, host, ship, launch, go live, or share a working link — "give me a link", "share it with friends", "make it live", "put it online", "host this". Takes a single self-contained HTML page, or a full app: a multi-file, framework-, or database-backed app runs as a runtime app with the services it declares (managed MongoDB, Redis, pgvector, disk, an AI gateway with no API key). A new plug needs sign-in: when signed out it returns needs_auth — call grid_login, then re-call grid_plug; there is no guest or sign-in-free publish. Create and update are the same call: without target_entity_id (or grid+slug) it CREATEs a new URL, with one it UPDATEs that URL in place. Pass exactly one source: `html`, `path` (local folder/file), or `artifact_files`. To edit a page without its HTML, call grid_get_app_source first, then deploy with target_entity_id.

html.description: A single self-contained HTML document to publish as an inspiration — the fast single-file path, live at a public URL in seconds. Pass the COMPLETE raw HTML inline (CSS+JS inline, images/fonts as data: URIs); a small fragment is wrapped into a full document. Do NOT base64-encode it, and do NOT pass an `@`-prefixed path or a file path here. Mutually exclusive with `path` and `artifact_files`. Materialized as one index.html in the signed-in user's grid.

filename.description: Filename for the single-file `html` path. Defaults to index.html.

path.description: Local edition: path to the entity folder, a single file, or a .zip ARCHIVE to upload. A folder is read recursively, honoring .gitignore/.cloudgridignore (plus .git/node_modules always skipped). A .zip is extracted and plugged: with its own cloudgrid.yaml it plugs as that project; otherwise it becomes a static app (all files served). Use this for "deploy this zip" / "gallery from these zipped images" requests. Mutually exclusive with `html` and `artifact_files` — EXCEPT `html` + a .zip of assets: the html becomes index.html over the archive's files (generate the page, let the zip supply the images).
Repo-relative path, e.g. index.html or services/web/index.js.

content.description: File content. Base64 when encoding is base64, otherwise UTF-8 text.

artifact_files.description: The source inline, one entry per file — for hosted/no-filesystem transports (a multi-file app). For a single HTML page prefer `html`. Prefer `path` on the local edition. Sent INLINE (copied through this call), so large files (lockfiles, binaries) can truncate and silently fail the build; for a real framework, a lockfile, or binary assets, the disk-based CLI (`npx -y @cloudgrid-io/cli plug` where it is already signed in) is more reliable — if you can only deploy inline and would have to omit large files, tell the user rather than dropping them silently. Mutually exclusive with `html` and `path`.

cloudgrid_yaml.description: Inline cloudgrid.yaml (the entity manifest). Optional — server auto-detection applies when omitted. On re-plug, a name: change is a warning only; it never renames the entity or moves the URL.

target_entity_id.description: Present → RE-PLUG: update this exact entity in place (same entity_id, slug, URL, plug history). Absent → CREATE a new entity. This is the durable handle a previous plug returned — persist it. Re-plugging a drop that was plugged outside a grid also needs its owner_token.

grid.description: On create: the grid slug to plug into. The destination grid is the USER'S CHOICE — treat it like visibility: NEVER infer one silently, and never reuse a previous or active grid without the user. If the user has more than one grid, CONFIRM which grid before plugging (omit this and grid_plug returns needs_grid with the grid list to choose from); a single-grid user is not asked. State the destination in the user's own terms ("plugging into <grid>") BEFORE the entity is created — a new entity in the wrong grid gets the wrong URL, is exposed to the wrong grid's members, and inherits the wrong datastore tier and namespace, and that is expensive to catch after the fact. On re-plug the entity never moves grids, but pass its home grid here when it differs from your active grid (the API checks your membership in the entity's grid). A drop plugged outside a grid stays outside until its owner claims it into one.

slug.description: Alternative RE-PLUG handle: paired with `grid`, resolves to an existing entity (the pickup contract's replug_handle) and updates it in place — for a client that holds only grid+slug, not the raw entity_id. target_entity_id takes precedence. A grid+slug that does NOT resolve to an existing entity is treated as a CREATE (never a false-positive re-plug).

url.description: Alternative RE-PLUG handle: the entity's public CloudGrid URL (e.g. https://<grid>.cloudgrid.io/<slug>) — use it to edit in place when you have the URL but no target_entity_id (the common "change the color of this page" flow after grid_get_app_source). The grid is read from the host and the entity is resolved via the pickup contract, so no `grid` param is needed. target_entity_id and grid+slug take precedence. A non-CloudGrid host is ignored (never redirects the write); a URL that does not resolve is treated as a CREATE.

kind.description: Force the detected kind; omit to let the server auto-detect.

yaml.description: An inline cloudgrid.yaml override used as a detection hint.

hints.description: Classification hints for the CREATE path (not entity targeting — that's target_entity_id).

anon.description: Deprecated — does not publish. A new plug needs sign-in: without it grid_plug returns needs_auth and publishes nothing, even with anon: true; when signed in it is ignored. Do not pass it. To edit a drop that was plugged outside a grid, pass target_entity_id + owner_token instead.

owner_token.description: The owner token of a drop plugged outside a grid — authorizes its re-plug (with target_entity_id). Re-minted on every such edit; always persist the newest one from the result.

confirm_new_app.description: Set true to confirm plugging a source that already contains a cloudgrid.yaml as a NEW runtime app. On a create, if the source has a cloudgrid.yaml and this is not set, grid_plug returns needs_confirmation so you can ask the user first (or use target_entity_id to re-plug an existing entity).

user_request.description: Local edition: a brief version of the user's request that led to this deploy, for the optional QA session log (dark unless this machine's operator set CLOUDGRID_QA_SLACK_WEBHOOK). Omit if the user asked not to share it.

session_note.description: Local edition: one short paragraph on what you built and why, for the optional QA session log.

tools.name: grid_get_app_source
tools.description: Retrieve the CURRENT deployed HTML of an inspiration/drop inline as text, so you can edit it and re-plug the SAME URL when you no longer have its source in context (e.g. the user asks to 'change the color' of a page — even in a fresh chat with only its URL). Defaults to this session's last drop; otherwise pass the public url (or grid+slug). Given just a URL with no session, it resolves the entity_id via the pickup contract and also returns the entity's kind, single_html, capabilities (replug/fork), and replug_handle — read those to decide whether to edit in place (single-HTML + capabilities.replug), fall back for a multi-file app/agent (use source_download_url + the local edition/CLI), or offer a copy (grid_pickup) when it isn't yours. For a multi-file or runtime (app/agent) source, use source_download_url, or grid_pull to get the files and link the folder. Reads the HTML from the API server-side; read-only, creates nothing.

entity_id.description: The drop's durable id. Defaults to this session's last drop.

url.description: The public URL of the drop (e.g. https://<grid>.cloudgrid.io/<slug>). Defaults to this session's last drop URL.

grid.description: Grid slug — used only to construct the URL when neither url nor session state is available.

slug.description: Entity slug — used with grid to construct the URL when neither url nor session state is available.

tools.name: grid_login
tools.description: Start a CLI-free CloudGrid sign-in. Use when the user wants to log in, sign in, or authenticate, or when a plug returned needs_auth. Returns a URL to open in the browser; then call grid_login_status to finish. Uses CloudGrid's existing OAuth.

tools.name: grid_login_status
tools.description: Finish a sign-in started by grid_login. Polls once: if you have completed the browser sign-in, it saves your session; otherwise it tells you to finish and try again.

code.description: The sign-in code. Defaults to the most recent grid_login.

tools.name: grid_visibility
tools.description: Change who can see a CloudGrid inspiration OR runtime app/agent. Simple modes: private (only the user), grid (everyone in their grid), link (anyone with the URL — add indexed: true to be findable by search engines). Finer control via the TWO AXES instead: inside (who in the grid: private | spaces | grid) and outside (reach beyond it: none | link | public), with require_signin for a members-only link and `spaces` for selected spaces. 'authenticated' is retired (it maps to a sign-in-required link). Use when the user wants to make something private, restrict who sees it, or open it up — including right after a drop, with no target id needed. Kind-aware routing across both surfaces. Defaults to the drop made in this session. Requires sign-in. Calls the API directly.

visibility.description: Simple mode: private | grid | link ('public' is an alias of link — pass indexed: true for search-findable; 'authenticated' is the retired alias for a sign-in-required link; 'space' needs the `spaces` list). Pass either this OR the inside/outside axes.

inside.description: Axis 1 — who in the grid can see it: private (only the user), spaces (selected spaces — pass `spaces`), or grid (everyone in the grid). Use together with `outside`, instead of `visibility`.

outside.description: Axis 2 — reach beyond the grid: none, link (anyone with the link; add require_signin: true for signed-in accounts only), or public (anyone, and findable by search engines).

require_signin.description: With outside: link (or visibility: link) — the link requires a signed-in CloudGrid account.

spaces.description: Space slugs, for inside: spaces (or the legacy space/grid modes).

indexed.description: With visibility: link — make the page search-engine indexable.

entity_id.description: Entity id. Defaults to this session's last drop.

kind.description: Entity kind. Omit to auto-detect from this session's last drop (falls back to trying the runtime surface, then the inspiration surface).

grid.description: Grid of the entity. Defaults to the active grid.

tools.name: grid_check_deploy
tools.description: Check whether an async runtime-app build has finished and the app is live. Call this after grid_plug returns status "building" — repeat every ~15s until it reports success or failed, and do NOT tell the user the app is live until it does. Defaults to this session's last deploy; pass poll_url from a grid_plug result to check another. Requires sign-in (builds are owned). Calls the API directly — works on every edition, including hosted.

poll_url.description: The poll_url from a grid_plug result. Defaults to this session's last deploy.

grid.description: Grid of the entity. Defaults to the deploy's grid, then the active grid.

tools.name: grid_list_grids
tools.description: List the signed-in user's grids, each with slug, name, role, and provisioning status. Requires sign-in. To plug onto a brand-new grid, call grid_plug right away: it waits for the grid to be ready itself, so do not poll render_ready or wait before plugging.

tools.name: grid_start
tools.description: A short orientation for building with CloudGrid: the account this session is signed in as and its active grid, how to choose between a single-page plug and a runtime app (and what each provides: managed database, Redis, pgvector, disk, an AI gateway with no API key), the sign-in and grid steps a first plug goes through, and the index of workflows to load with grid_get_template. Read-only, under 3,000 characters; useful once per session before the first plug. The full operating playbook is grid_get_template({kind:"doc", name:"playbook"}).

tools.name: grid_get_template
tools.description: Load a specific CloudGrid workflow, template, example, rule, troubleshooting note, or reference doc by name — deterministic retrieval from the bundled corpus, no network. Workflows and templates come from the index grid_start returns, e.g. grid_get_template({kind:"workflow", name:"presentation"}) then grid_get_template({kind:"template", name:"deck"}). Reference docs: cloudgrid-yaml (the manifest schema and needs: vocabulary), capability-map (which template fits a request), playbook (the full operating rules).

tools.name: grid_report
tools.description: Report a genuine CloudGrid failure to the CloudGrid team — ONLY with the user's explicit consent. When a build/deploy or platform call fails unexpectedly, ASK the user first; call this only after they say yes. What is sent: the short `message` (what failed), the `context` you pass (the tool, inputs, grid, original request, error code/detail), and the client name and platform — nothing else from the conversation. include_conversation:true adds the chat, and is set ONLY if the user explicitly agreed to send it. Redaction is key-name-only: a value is dropped only when its KEY looks secret, so a secret embedded in a value (e.g. inside HTML) is NOT redacted — do not put secrets in `message` or `context`. Never sends anything the user didn't agree to.

message.description: Short summary of what failed (required). Do not paste the whole conversation here.

tool.description: The CloudGrid tool that failed, e.g. grid_plug.

inputs.description: The failing inputs (e.g. the HTML/args). Keep it minimal and do NOT include secrets — a secret embedded in a value here is not redacted.

grid.description: The grid/org slug involved, if any.

original_request.description: What the user asked for, in one line.

error_code.description: The server error code, e.g. INTERNAL_ERROR.

error_detail.description: The error message / detail surfaced to the agent.

context.description: The failed-request context. Redaction is key-name-only (a value is dropped only when its KEY looks secret) client-side, and the server applies the same key-name filter — a secret embedded in a value is not redacted by either.

include_conversation.description: Default false. Set true ONLY if the user explicitly agreed to include the full conversation.

category.description: Optional category, e.g. the failing tool name ("deploy"). Defaults to "mcp".

trace_id.description: The server's trace/deploy id from the failed response, if any (helps support pivot to the trace).

failed_step.description: The server-side pipeline step that failed, if known.

http_status.description: The HTTP status of the final failed request, if applicable.

tools.name: grid_hello
tools.description: Create a minimal hello page and plug it into the user's grid, returning the live URL. If the user has more than one grid and `grid` is not given, this returns needs_grid with the list — ASK the user which grid, then call again with `grid` set. Never guess the grid. Requires sign-in.

grid.description: Grid slug to plug into. Omit on the first call to be asked.

tools.name: grid_create_project
tools.description: Scaffold a new CloudGrid app or agent folder (cloudgrid.yaml + a web service), optionally pre-declaring resources. Wraps `grid new` (scaffolds locally; no server entity until you grid_plug). Language note: the nextjs starter is TypeScript (writes tsconfig.json + app/*.tsx), but CloudGrid templates are plain JavaScript. When you fill a template, treat the template's files as the source of truth — delete the scaffolded tsconfig.json and app/*.tsx, then write the template's .js files. Never leave both .tsx and .js for the same route.

kind.description: Entity kind. 'agent' scaffolds an agent: block.

type.description: Seed a web service of this type.

needs.description: Pre-declare infrastructure needs in the scaffolded cloudgrid.yaml (e.g. ["database","ai"]).

dir.description: Target directory. Defaults to the current folder.

grid.description: Override the active grid this project will target.

cwd.description: Working directory. The CLI runs in this directory. Defaults to the MCP server's working directory.

tools.name: grid_view_logs
tools.description: Tail recent logs for an entity. Does not stream; returns a snapshot. Wraps `grid logs`.

name.description: Entity name. Omit to use the entity linked to the current directory.

since.description: Only logs newer than this, e.g. 5m, 1h, 2d.

tools.name: grid_share
tools.description: Set an entity's visibility and print its URL. Defaults to link (anyone with the URL). Wraps `grid visibility set`.

tools.name: grid_feedback
tools.description: List recent feedback events for the active grid. Read-only. Wraps `grid feedback list`.

since.description: Only events newer than this, e.g. 24h, 7d.

grid.description: Read another grid's feed where you have access.

tools.name: grid_whoami
tools.description: Show the signed-in user and active grid. Wraps `grid whoami`.

tools.name: grid_switch_grid
tools.description: Switch the active grid. Wraps `grid use`.

tools.name: grid_logout
tools.description: Sign out and clear local credentials. Wraps `grid logout`.

tools.name: grid_status
tools.description: Grid dashboard, entity detail, or deploy snapshot. Wraps `grid status`.

name.description: Entity name or trace id. Omit for the org dashboard.

tools.name: grid_info
tools.description: Show metadata for a CloudGrid entity. Wraps `grid info`.

name.description: Entity name. Omit for the entity linked to the current directory.

tools.name: grid_get
tools.description: List CloudGrid grids, entities, or spaces. Wraps `grid get <grids|entities|spaces> --json`.

resource.description: What to list: grids, entities, or spaces.

grid.description: Grid slug (entities/spaces only). Omit for the active grid.

space.description: Only entities scoped to this space slug (entities only).

tools.name: grid_describe_grid
tools.description: Show a grid's detail: role, members, spaces, tier, wildcard-TLS state. Wraps `grid describe grid <slug> --json`.

tools.name: grid_edit_existing_app
tools.description: Continue/edit an EXISTING entity locally: download its source + cloudgrid.yaml and link the folder so your next `grid plug` updates it IN PLACE. Requires push access (owner or collaborator). Wraps `grid pull`. To make your own separate copy (a fork) instead, use grid_pickup. To GET push access to an entity you can currently only view, that is a different operation — grid_collab (CLI equivalent: `grid collab <entity>`), which grants permission only; run the pull again once it is granted.

name.description: Entity slug or id to pull.

target_dir.description: Directory to pull into (relative to cwd). Defaults to the entity name.

grid.description: Grid to resolve the entity in. Defaults to the active grid.

version.description: Pull an older version's source instead of HEAD.

no_bind.description: Download source only — skip cloudgrid.yaml and the link.

cwd.description: Working directory the CLI runs in. The download lands here; pass an explicit, writable directory.

tools.name: grid_rename
tools.description: Rename a CloudGrid entity's display name (slug stays the same). Wraps `grid rename`.

tools.name: grid_take_offline
tools.description: Take an entity off the grid. Destructive. Wraps `grid unplug`.

tools.name: grid_delete
tools.description: Archive a CloudGrid inspiration. Destructive. Wraps `grid delete entity`.

tools.name: grid_rollback_deploy
tools.description: Rollback an entity to a previous version. Wraps `grid rollback`.

to.description: Target version tag or id. Omit to roll back one version.

tools.name: grid_list_versions
tools.description: List published versions for an entity. Wraps `grid versions`.

name.description: Entity name. Omit for the entity linked to the current directory.

tools.name: grid_set_env
tools.description: Manage environment variables for an entity. Wraps `grid env`.

key.description: Variable name. Required for get and set.

cwd.description: Working directory. The CLI runs in this directory. Defaults to the MCP server's working directory.

tools.name: grid_set_secret
tools.description: Set or list secret names for an entity. Never returns secret values. Wraps `grid secrets`.

cwd.description: Working directory. The CLI runs in this directory. Defaults to the MCP server's working directory.

tools.description: Scaffold service folders declared in cloudgrid.yaml (idempotent). Wraps `grid scaffold`.

cwd.description: Working directory. The CLI runs in this directory. Defaults to the MCP server's working directory.

tools.description: Run CloudGrid diagnostics on the local environment. Wraps `grid doctor`.

tools.name: grid_get_url
tools.description: Return the public URL for an entity. Does not open a browser. Wraps `grid open --print`.

instructions:
CloudGrid runs the user's web apps at a live public URL and provides the infrastructure they need: managed MongoDB, Redis, pgvector, persistent disk, and an AI gateway that needs no API key. Every tool here is grid_*.

What it does, and the requests each tool serves:
- One self-contained HTML file becomes a live public URL in seconds: grid_plug with html (or path to the file). Serves "make it live", "put it online", "give me a link", "share it with friends", "plug it".
- A folder with several files, a framework, or anything that needs a database, a server, scheduled jobs, or an AI model, runs as a runtime app: grid_plug with path to the folder, with a cloudgrid.yaml that declares needs (needs: { database: true }, needs: { ai: true }); read the injected env vars lazily, inside handlers. Serves "deploy this app", "add a database", "let it call an AI model without my own key".
- Iterating keeps the same link: grid_plug with target_entity_id updates in place.
- Sharing and access: grid_visibility sets who can see it; grid_collab grants push access; grid_pickup copies any visible app's source.

What it does not do: it is not a shell, a container or VM host, or a Kubernetes target; it does not deploy a git repository from a URL; it does not run desktop or mobile apps.

How a plug works: creating anything needs a signed-in account (a signed-out create returns needs_auth; call grid_login). Never write an API key into page source or app code — needs: { ai: true } gives the app the managed AI gateway with no key, and other keys go in grid secrets (grid_plug rejects known key shapes). A runtime build is asynchronous: poll grid_check_deploy until success before saying it is live. For shell steps, run the CLI as `npx -y @cloudgrid-io/cli@latest <command>` (never a bare `grid`); `grid dev` runs the app locally with the same services. grid_start returns a short orientation and the workflow index; grid_get_template loads workflows, templates, and reference docs.
